capabilities.target: CRM customer record, lookup by email or account id, any customer

instructions.note: Agent is told it 'may look up any customer by email or account id' with no check that the requester is the owner of that account.
Routine tickets are sent directly with no human review; the only escalation condition is the model's own judgment of whether the customer 'is angry', which is not a structural gate.
The sole safeguard against cross-customer disclosure is a natural-language rule ('Never share another customer's information'), a dependent behavioral control with no structural backing.
Agent is implicitly authorized to send external email on the company's behalf for the common case with no human in the loop.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model reading and obeying a natural-language rule while processing the very untrusted email that may try to override it; a more capable model follows longer, more convincing injected goals and can reason its way to exceptions.

controls.name: Escalate to human only if the customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The model itself judges emotional tone and decides whether to escalate; a calmly worded malicious request bypasses it entirely, and a more capable model becomes more persuasive at appearing calm/compliant with the injected goal.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging infrastructure operates independent of model behavior, but it is purely detective and occurs after the email has already left, so it earns no preventive credit.

controls.name: Per-request scoped CRM credential bound to the verified ticket requester
controls.decay_rationale: Would not decay with model capability because access to other customers' records would be structurally unreachable, not merely discouraged.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's system-of-record requester address
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the send destination to the verified requester address from the ticketing system, rather than any model-chosen address, would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate before sending email containing another account's data
controls.decay_rationale: A structural gate reviewed as raw_action does not decay with model behavior and would not be subject to ASI09 summary-gaming.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives cross-customer CRM read and unscoped email send

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email requests lookup of an arbitrary customer's account; prompt.md:3 permits lookup by email or account id with no ownership check.
Agent retrieves the targeted customer's confidential record using a broad-scope service credential (CRM_SVC_TOKEN reads every record).
Agent drafts and autonomously sends a reply containing that data to any address via a shared service account, with no approval gate.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version string in runtime config changes, or subject.model.swappable remains true with no review gate added; the design already declares platform-driven auto-upgrade with no separate review.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed it 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' with no check that the requester owns that account.
Agent sends routine responses directly without human review, escalating only on perceived anger.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both reached with static bearer tokens; no per-user scoping visible in config.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential per request to the verified identity of the ticket's own requester rather than a single broad service token.
Bind the outbound recipient to the address of record for the ticket instead of allowing the model to choose or confirm arbitrary destinations.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any email leaves the system when the drafted content includes another account's identifying data.
Alert, not just log, on any outbound email whose recipient domain does not match the inbound ticket's requester domain.

findings.title: Confused deputy (ASI03): shared, unscoped service credentials grant every session brokerage-wide CRM and send authority

attack_path.note: Any inbound ticket runs under the same CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN regardless of which customer is emailing.
Credential scope is broad: full CRM read access, not scoped to the requester's own account.
Credential scope is a shared service account that can send to any address, not scoped to the ticket's requester.

forecast.watch_signal: New CRM data sources or mailboxes added to the shared service accounts, or the model upgraded without corresponding credential re-scoping.

evidence.observation: CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account. It can send to any address.
Both servers are configured with a single static bearer token per server, not a token scoped per user or per ticket.

recommendations.action: Issue per-user or per-ticket scoped tokens instead of a single broad shared service account for both CRM and mail.
Add anomaly detection on CRM read volume and pattern per agent session to catch bulk or out-of-pattern lookups.

rating.rationale: Both findings share one path: an untrusted inbound email can direct a CRM read of any customer's confidential record and an autonomous, irreversible external email send (S3 sink), giving inherent risk of critical under the U-to-S3 base matrix; the autonomy modifier also applies because both max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are null. The only preventive controls present are two behavioral, capability-dependent prompt instructions (do not share other customers' data; escalate only if the customer seems angry). Per rubric step 4 these earn a single, capped -1 tier credit, giving a residual of high. No structural control severs, gates, or scopes the path today: the CRM credential is broad, the mail credential is a shared service account that can send anywhere, and SIEM logging is detective-only and occurs after disclosure. Because the design explicitly upgrades the model with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable), the model_upgrade trigger defeats both dependent instructions, and the forecast reverts to critical. The credential-scoping recommendations are the highest-leverage fix because they are structural and severing rather than behavioral.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the provided runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No IaC, tool schema, or agent card artifacts were provided; capability scope and MCP server trust are inferred from mcp.json headers and the runtime notes, so protocol-level authentication and definition-pinning claims are marked unverified (peer_identity_verified: false, definitions_pinned: false) rather than confirmed absent.

No approval gate configuration was found; the design is scored as A3 with no approval control because prompt.md's escalation condition ('unless the customer is angry') is behavioral, not a structural approval gate.
Attack paths are limited to the two declared capabilities (CRM read, email send); if additional CRM or mail actions exist outside these artifacts they are not assessed.
